run.question:
Alertmanager alert RequestErrorRate (severity warning) is firing for service otel-demo/checkout since 2026-11-16T12:37:58Z.
Investigate why this alert is firing.

report.summary: The RequestErrorRate alert for otel-demo/checkout is firing because checkout's oteldemo.CheckoutService/PlaceOrder spans return ERROR: the error-status span rate left 0 at 12:38:58Z, reached ~0.43/s by 12:45Z, plateaued near 0.47/s between 12:53Z and 13:08Z and was still ~0.22/s at 13:16:58Z, so roughly a quarter to a half of order attempts failed during the alert window. Every sampled failure carries the same description, 'shipping quote failure: failed POST to email service: expected 200, got 400', with rpc.grpc.status_code=13, and the same failed subtrace: checkout's outbound 'HTTP POST' span is marked ERROR and is the parent of the shipping '/get-quote' server span, which answers in 31-469 microseconds with no 'POST quote' client span and no quote-service span. A successful order in the same minute shows the healthy shape (checkout 'HTTP POST' 36.9 ms -> shipping '/get-quote' 36.4 ms -> shipping 'POST quote' 36.3 ms -> quote 'POST /getquote' 444 us). Per-minute span counts confirm the arithmetic: 162 PlaceOrder attempts and 166 shipping '/get-quote' spans, but only 110 complete orders reach shipping 'POST quote' (110), quote (106) and email (106). So shipping's quote endpoint rejects about a third of requests in under a millisecond, before calling the quote service, and checkout surfaces that as a non-200 POST failure. The stated reason for the rejection is not recorded by shipping (its '/get-quote' spans have no status tags, and no error lines were found in its logs). The email service is not the failing dependency despite the wording of checkout's message: email only ever serves 'POST /send_order_confirmation' with http.status_code=200, has no ERROR series, and its request rate equals only the successful orders. Downstream, frontend, frontend-proxy and load-generator show their own ERROR spans with http.status_code=500 on the checkout path. cart, currency, product-catalog, payment, accounting, quote and email show no error-status spans. The only other change in the window is the load-generator Deployment rollout at 13:02:04Z, which no evidence ties to this failure.

claims.text: checkout's ERROR span rate on span_name 'HTTP POST' and on 'oteldemo.CheckoutService/PlaceOrder' is identical: 0 at 12:37:58Z, 0.0137 at 12:38:58Z, 0.0463 at 12:39:58Z, 0.233 at 12:41:58Z, 0.4259 at 12:43:58Z, a ~0.45-0.52 plateau from 12:45Z to 12:53Z, a dip to 0.0926 at 12:56:58Z, then 0.1594 at 12:57:58Z rising to 0.2838 at 13:02:58Z and 0.2202 at 13:16:58Z - matching the alert start time and its 'current: 0.19999...' annotation.

At 12:45Z checkout had 0.4259/s ERROR spans on 'HTTP POST' and 0.4259/s on 'oteldemo.CheckoutService/PlaceOrder' against 0.7852/s UNSET PlaceOrder spans, while checkout's other client spans (CartService/GetCart 1.20/s, CartService/EmptyCart 0.785/s, CurrencyService/Convert 1.95/s, PaymentService/Charge 0.785/s, ProductCatalogService/GetProduct 1.17/s, orders publish 0.785/s) had no ERROR series.

Sampled failing traces at 12:40-12:44Z show checkout 'oteldemo.CheckoutService/PlaceOrder' with error=true, otel.status_code=ERROR, rpc.grpc.status_code=13 and status description / exception.message 'shipping quote failure: failed POST to email service: expected 200, got 400'; the same traces carry frontend 'POST /api/checkout' and 'executing api route (pages) /api/checkout' spans with http.status_code=500, frontend 'grpc.oteldemo.CheckoutService/PlaceOrder' with grpc.error_message '13 INTERNAL: shipping quote failure: failed POST to email service: expected 200, got 400', frontend-proxy 'ingress' and 'router frontend egress' spans with http.status_code=500, and load-generator 'POST' spans with http.status_code=500.

In whole trace fabf30c40bb674e79e93dd78836bb231 (12:42:37Z) the failed order contains a single outbound call attempt: checkout 'HTTP POST' (826 us, error=true, otel.status_code=ERROR) whose supplied parent reference is the trace-level checkout PlaceOrder span, with shipping '/get-quote' (469 us, no status tags) as its child; there is no email span, no product-catalog/currency/payment span and no shipping 'POST quote' span in that trace.

A successful order in the same minute (trace f7f1b65fab2be85f05e0abffd1916040) shows the healthy dependency chain: checkout 'HTTP POST' 36881 us -> shipping '/get-quote' 36421 us -> shipping 'POST quote' 36263 us -> quote 'POST /getquote' 444 us; a second checkout 'HTTP POST' 5179 us -> email 'POST /send_order_confirmation' 4370 us with http.status_code=200; a third 'HTTP POST' 457 us -> shipping '/ship-order' 36 us; PlaceOrder completed with rpc.grpc.status_code=0 and frontend returned http.status_code=200.

Span counts for 12:42:30-12:43:30Z: checkout PlaceOrder 162 and 'HTTP POST' 382; shipping '/get-quote' 166, 'POST quote' 110, '/ship-order' 108; quote 'POST /getquote' 106; email 'POST /send_order_confirmation' 106; checkout CartService/GetCart 162, CartService/EmptyCart 110, PaymentService/Charge 110. Every order attempt reaches shipping '/get-quote', but only completed orders proceed to quote, email and ship-order.

Across 8 sampled failing traces (12:42:00-12:42:37Z) the shipping '/get-quote' children of the failed checkout POSTs last 31, 37, 38, 41, 45, 45, 48 and 469 microseconds and carry no status tags - sub-millisecond responses, versus 36.4 ms for the successful order that includes the quote round-trip.

The quote service exists as its own service_name in the span metrics, with only the operations 'POST /getquote', 'calculate-quote' and '{closure}', at 0.761/s each at 12:50Z with STATUS_CODE_UNSET; shipping exposes three operations, '/get-quote' and '/ship-order' as server spans and 'POST quote' as its client span to quote.

The email service is not erroring in this window: its only server operation is 'POST /send_order_confirmation' (plus send_email, sinatra.render_template), all its span series are STATUS_CODE_UNSET with no ERROR series at 12:50Z, it served 0.754/s requests while checkout made 0.858/s successful plus 0.426/s failed PlaceOrder attempts, its request volume in 12:42:30-12:43:30Z was 106 versus 162 checkout order attempts, and checkout logs show repeated success lines such as 'order confirmation email sent to \"jack@example.com\"' at 13:09Z.

The quote service, shipping's dependency, is healthy in the observed window: at 12:50Z its three operations show 0.761/s each with only STATUS_CODE_UNSET, no ERROR series exists for service_name=quote, and its request rate (106/min in 12:42:30-12:43:30Z) matches the successful-order rate rather than the 166/min of shipping '/get-quote' requests.

Error-status span counts over 11:40:53-13:17:53Z exist only for checkout (1732), frontend (3246), frontend-proxy (53374), ad (3.06), fraud-detection (3.05) and recommendation (4.06), while accounting and payment report 0; no error-status series was returned for cart, currency, product-catalog, shipping, quote or email.

The pods involved were healthy at the object level: checkout-5dccddf8bb-vh65b, shipping-75d58f5d84-kgmz9, email-59f69bc6cf-7wqqk and quote-6b5877698d-x6v2f were Running and ready with 0 restarts, started 12:27:49-12:27:51Z (all application pods except load-generator started 12:27-12:29Z); checkout's container working set was ~13.8 MB and shipping's ~3.6 MB at 13:15Z.

The visible flagd configuration (configmap flagd-config, file demo.flagd.json) has every fault flag at its 'off' default: adFailure, adHighCpu, cartFailure, paymentFailure, paymentUnreachable, productCatalogFailure, recommendationCacheFailure, emailMemoryLeak, imageSlowLoad, kafkaQueueProblems are all off, and no checkout/shipping/quote failure flag is defined there; only loadGeneratorFloodHomepage has a non-zero default (100).

shipping's captured log lines during the failure burst are only its three normal messages: 57 'Requesting quote' and 57 'Sending Quote' lines between 12:42:30 and 12:43:30Z, and a 12:42:36-12:42:39Z slice showing 'Requesting quote' -> 'Sending Quote' -> 'Tracking ID Created' sequences at 12:42:37.353Z and 12:42:37.889Z. The failing request at 12:42:37.586Z falls between those two logged sequences, with no failure line captured in that slice.

checkout's configuration targets two distinct endpoints, EMAIL_ADDR=http://email:8080 and SHIPPING_ADDR=http://shipping:8080 (image ghcr.io/open-telemetry/demo:2.1.3-checkout), and the otel-demo Services email (100.65.212.222:8080, selector opentelemetry.io/name=email) and shipping (100.70.79.245:8080, selector opentelemetry.io/name=shipping) differ, so no service-selector misrouting explains a shipping quote call being served by email.

A Deployment/load-generator rollout occurred at 13:02:04Z: ReplicaSet load-generator-7d5756fbd9 scaled 0->1 with SuccessfulCreate of pod load-generator-7d5756fbd9-zzj4z, and ReplicaSet load-generator-c7cbc4c99 scaled 1->0 with SuccessfulDelete of load-generator-c7cbc4c99-xlnk2 at 13:02:05Z; the new pod shows 0 restarts and start time 13:02:04Z.

Most likely deep cause: the shipping service's '/get-quote' endpoint accepts every quote request (a server span exists for all 166 attempts/min) but answers roughly one third of them with a non-200 status in under 1 ms, before calling the quote service (no 'POST quote' child span; quote traffic equals only the successful-order rate; shipping '/get-quote' spans carry no error status of their own). The status value 400 is stated by checkout's own error text ('expected 200, got 400'), so the failing dependency response originates at shipping's quote endpoint; whether shipping is rejecting an invalid request body or wrongly rejecting valid requests cannot be decided from the available telemetry.

Remaining alternative: the fault originates on the checkout side, i.e. checkout sends quote request bodies that shipping rejects at the HTTP/JSON layer, since checkout's other POSTs (ship-order and send_order_confirmation) succeed with 2xx in the sampled successful trace. This is not separable from a shipping-side validation defect with the available telemetry because no request payload or 400 response body is captured.

The hypothesis that the email service returned the 400 named in the checkout error text was rejected: email has no ERROR spans, its 'POST /send_order_confirmation' spans record http.status_code=200, its request rate equals only the successful-order count (106/min versus 162 attempts/min), and the sampled failing traces contain no email span while the failing checkout POST span's supplied child is shipping '/get-quote'. The 'email service' wording in the error string is therefore not corroborated by the email service's own evidence.

Hypotheses of cart, currency, product-catalog, payment or kafka failure as the cause were rejected: no error-status span series exist for cart, currency, product-catalog, shipping, quote or email; PaymentService/Charge and CartService/EmptyCart occur exactly as often as completed orders (110/min in 12:42:30-12:43:30Z); payment and accounting report 0 error spans; and checkout log lines during the window are 'Successful to write message. offset: 0, duration: 147.404µs' (12:37:54Z) and 'Successful to write message. offset: 0, duration: 154.404µs' (12:47:43Z).

This Prometheus exposes only 63 metric names, of which the trace metrics are 'traces_span_metrics_calls_total' and 'traces_span_metrics_duration_milliseconds_bucket'; no HTTP server or gRPC client request metrics (for example http_server_request_duration_seconds_count or rpc_client_duration_milliseconds_count) are present.

gaps: The reason shipping's '/get-quote' returns a non-200 is not recorded: shipping's own spans carry no status tag, and a filtered read of shipping logs excluding its three normal messages returned no data (status no_data), so no error or warning line was observed - but that absence is not proof that no such line exists.

No non-Normal Kubernetes events were observed for otel-demo, but the events query filtered to type != Normal returned status no_data, so this cannot be treated as a clean bill of health for pod events.

The checkout error text names the 'email service' while the failing call is observed to target shipping '/get-quote'; the discrepancy is unexplained and checkout's application source could not be read to confirm the wording's origin.

Jaeger's in-memory store only held traces up to 12:42:48Z; later searches for checkout error traces in 12:45-12:50Z and 13:02-13:05Z returned nothing (no_data), so no failing trace after 12:43Z could be sampled and the late-window error rate is known only from span metrics.
Server-side HTTP status codes and 4xx counts per service could not be verified independently of traces because this Prometheus exposes no such metric families.
The RequestErrorRate alerting rule is not visible in this Prometheus (rule lookup by name returned no data), so its exact expression, threshold and evaluation interval are unknown.

The change_history integration is not available in this Run, so no record of configuration or application changes near 12:37-12:40Z could be checked; all workload pods except load-generator predate the alert (started 12:27-12:29Z).

A filtered read of quote logs for 'error|fail|400' returned only 'Calculated quote' lines, so no quote-side error text was observed, but the filter matched on the word 'quote' and cannot prove absence of errors.

shipping log line counts do not reconcile with span counts (about 57 quote log lines per minute versus 166 '/get-quote' spans per minute), so the absence of handler log lines for failing requests cannot locate where shipping rejects them.

ad (about 3 error spans), fraud-detection (about 3) and recommendation (about 4) show a very small number of error-status spans over 97 minutes; these were not investigated and no evidence ties them to the checkout failures.
next_steps: Read the checkout HTTP client code that emits 'failed POST to X service: expected 200, got N' to confirm whether the 'email service' wording is a mislabel for the shipping quote POST, and capture the exact request body sent to shipping '/get-quote'.

Review shipping's '/get-quote' request validation (for example behaviour on an empty items array or missing address fields) and enable request-level debug logging so the 400 response body is captured for failing requests.

Compare checkout's quote request schema with the shipping image (ghcr.io/open-telemetry/demo:2.1.3-shipping) expectations and verify that checkout, shipping and quote images did not drift from the intended 2.1.3 set.
Check change history or deployment records (integration not available here) for anything changed on shipping or checkout around 12:37-12:40Z, when the error rate left zero.

view.series_note: traces_span_metrics_calls_total counts spans of every operation of the service (internal, client and server spans alike), summed over the labels kept in this query; it is not a count of requests. status_code STATUS_CODE_UNSET means the span carried no status; it does not mean the call succeeded.

view.cannot_prove: Objects are the cluster's state when the query ran, not during the incident window: they cannot prove what was true earlier, and an object missing now may have existed then. Events cover only their own timestamps inside the window; an event that is not returned is unknown, not proof nothing happened (events expire and timestamps are often null). <none> means the path reached no value in that object, not that the field is absent from the kind; a filtered table is not a full picture of the kind.

    endpoint: ${env:MY_POD_IP}:13133
processors:
  batch: {}
  k8sattributes:
    extract:
      metadata:
      - k8s.namespace.name
      - k8s.deployment.name
      - k8s.statefulset.name
      - k8s.daemonset.name
      - k8s.cronjob.name
      - k8s.job.name
      - k8s.node.name
      - k8s.pod.name
      - k8s.pod.uid
      - k8s.pod.start_time
    passthrough: false
    pod_association:
    - sources:
      - from: resource_attribute
        name: k8s.pod.ip
    - sources:
      - from: resource_attribute
        name: k8s.pod.uid
    - sources:
      - from: connection
  memory_limiter:
    check_interval: 5s
    limit_percentage: 80
    spike_limit_percentage: 25
  resource:
    attributes:
    - action: insert
      from_attribute: k8s.pod.uid
      key: service.instance.id
  resourcedetection:
    detectors:
    - env
    - system
  transform:
    error_mode: ignore
    trace_statements:
    - context: span
      statements:
      - replace_pattern(name, "\\?.*", "")
      - replace_match(name, "GET /api/products/*", "GET /api/products/{productId}")
receivers:
  httpcheck/frontend-proxy:
    targets:
    - endpoint: http://frontend-proxy:8080
  jaeger:
    protocols:
      grpc:
        endpoint: ${env:MY_POD_IP}:14250
      thrift_compact:
        endpoint: ${env:MY_POD_IP}:6831
      thrift_http:
        endpoint: ${env:MY_POD_IP}:14268
  nginx:
    collection_interval: 10s
    endpoint: http://image-provider:8081/status
  otlp:
    protocols:
      grpc:
        endpoint: ${env:MY_POD_IP}:4317
      http:
        cors:
          allowed_origins:
          - http://*
          - https://*
        endpoint: ${env:MY_POD_IP}:4318
  postgresql:
    endpoint: postgresql:5432
    metrics:
      postgresql.blks_hit:
        enabled: true
      postgresql.blks_read:
        enabled: true
      postgresql.deadlocks:
        enabled: true
      postgresql.tup_deleted:
        enabled: true
      postgresql.tup_fetched:
        enabled: true
      postgresql.tup_inserted:
        enabled: true
      postgresql.tup_returned:
        enabled: true
      postgresql.tup_updated:
        enabled: true
    password: [REDACTED_CREDENTIAL]
    tls:
      insecure: true
    username: root
  prometheus:
    config:
      scrape_configs:
      - job_name: opentelemetry-collector
        scrape_interval: 10s
        static_configs:
        - targets:
          - ${env:MY_POD_IP}:8888
  redis:
    collection_interval: 10s
    endpoint: valkey-cart:6379
    username: valkey
  zipkin:
    endpoint: ${env:MY_POD_IP}:9411
service:
  extensions:
  - health_check
  pipelines:
    logs:
      exporters:
      - clickhouse
      - debug
      processors:
      - k8sattributes
      - memory_limiter
      - resourcedetection
      - resource
      - batch
      receivers:
      - otlp
    metrics:
      exporters:
      - debug
      - prometheus
      processors:
      - k8sattributes
      - memory_limiter
      - resourcedetection
      - resource
      - batch
      receivers:
      - httpcheck/frontend-proxy
      - nginx
      - otlp
      - postgresql
      - redis
      - spanmetrics
    traces:
      exporters:
      - clickhouse
      - debug
      - otlp
      - spanmetrics
      processors:
      - k8sattributes
      - memory_limiter
      - resourcedetection
      - resource
      - transform
      - batch
      receivers:
      - otlp
      - jaeger
      - zipkin
  telemetry:
    metrics:
      level: detailed
      readers:
      - pull:
          exporter:
            prometheus:
              host: 0.0.0.0
              port: 8888
